| # How to implement CAN legacy using Transmit, Receive Databoxes {#how-to-implement-can-legacy-using-transmit-receive-databoxes-1 .p_Heading1 style="page-break-after: avoid;"} |                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Following examples suggest how to configure and use CAN related parameters such as number of databoxes, along with baud rate configuration, if databox usage is preferred.

## Using Transmit/Receive Databox: {#using-transmitreceive-databox .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

## Example 1: Configure all CAN 2.0 related parameters in easyConfig and use BSW APIs for communication. {#example-1-configure-all-can-2.0-related-parameters-in-easyconfig-and-use-bsw-apis-for-communication. .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

### Step 1: {#step-1 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure a CAN channel for CAN 2.0 during pre-compile time (configuration in easyConfig).

in Communication \--\> Select CAN Channel

### Step 2: {#step-2 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure CAN baudrate for the selected CAN channel.

After selecting the CAN Channel, under settings(CAN/CAN-FD) choose CAN 2.0 and then configure the desired baudrate.

### Step 3: {#step-3 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Configure transmit and receive databox numbers for CAN 2.0 in the Legacy section.

### Step 4: {#step-4 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

In ASW, initialize CAN Transmit Databox(es) by calling  bds_can_initTxDatabox().

### Step 5: {#step-5 .p_Heading3 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

In ASW, initialize CAN Receive Databox(es) by calling  bds_can_initRxDatabox().
